title: Identity
normative_text: The language MUST be named TriX, preserving capital T and X. Pronouns referring to TriX MUST use the feminine forms she and her in English. This convention does not change the grammatical reference to a compiler, runtime component or artifact. Technical identifiers MAY use the normalisation required by their format.

title: Purpose
normative_text: TriX MUST support describing, validating, planning, executing and observing distributed work, including AI models, tools and data processing. She MUST make authority, data location, compatibility and resource conditions explicit.

title: Independence
normative_text: The language, central protocol and project data MUST NOT require one exclusive hardware vendor, operating system, model provider or cluster manager. A specialised extension MAY depend on a vendor if that dependency is declared.

title: Project continuity
normative_text: Infrastructure changes MUST preserve programs and projects whose semantics and requirements remain satisfied. When a new installation cannot meet a requirement, TriX MUST explain the incompatibility before initiating the affected task's effects.

title: Documentation language
normative_text: All authoritative project documentation, specifications, schemas, examples, comments intended for publication, diagnostics catalogues, decision records and implementer instructions MUST be maintained in English. Project documentation in another language requires an explicit later change to this instruction. User interfaces MAY be localised; their authoritative specifications and translation instructions remain in English.

title: Adopted revision
normative_text: Each implementation MUST declare its specification revision and conformance profiles. The project authority MUST record adoption and subsequent changes. The existence of this document alone does not constitute formal adoption.

title: Traceability
normative_text: Requirement identifiers MUST remain stable. Deliveries MUST connect applicable requirements to implementation, tests and limitations. Retired requirements MUST be marked superseded or withdrawn; their identifiers MUST NOT be reused.

title: Decisions
normative_text: Changes affecting semantics, authority, compatibility or guarantees MUST have an architecture decision record, or ADR, covering motivation, alternatives, impact, migration and validation evidence.

title: Profiles
normative_text: Conformance MUST distinguish the language core, coordination, local execution, distributed execution, remote access and control clients. Each profile MUST publish mandatory requirements, optional capabilities and profile dependencies before any conformance claim. An implementation MUST NOT exclude requirements needed by functionality it exposes.

title: Exceptions
normative_text: Exceptions to recommendations MUST have recorded reasons. An implementation violating a mandatory requirement MUST NOT claim complete conformance for the affected profile. Pending decisions MUST be resolved before the associated capability becomes stable.

title: Document precedence
normative_text: For revision 0.2, the numbered English requirements and explicit normative tables in this standard govern behaviour. Companion JSON Schemas govern the structural constraints they express. Examples, templates and generated registers do not override either. A contradiction MUST block the affected conformance claim until a versioned correction resolves it; an implementer MUST NOT silently choose the easier interpretation.

title: Evidence status
normative_text: Every capability, decision and test record MUST distinguish proposed, implemented and verified status. A successful document-package check MUST NOT be reported as a TriX runtime, compiler, security or hardware test. Claims MUST identify what was actually executed and what remains untested.

title: Initial subset
normative_text: The first implementation MUST support task contracts, dependencies, policies and execution through adapters. The project SHOULD validate this subset through an SDK, verifiable plans and executors before investing in a general-purpose compiler.

title: Separation of responsibilities
normative_text: The specification MUST separate language semantics, plan representation, runtime, adapters and developer tools. A graphical-interface decision MUST NOT change a program's meaning.

title: Reference implementation
normative_text: A Rust coordination and execution core, isolated Python integration adapters and Swift clients on Apple platforms are RECOMMENDED. This composition MUST remain an implementation choice; extensions MUST NOT be required to use these languages solely to participate.

title: Reuse
normative_text: Existing engines, compilers and distribution mechanisms SHOULD be reused where they satisfy the contracts. A new low-level backend or custom kernel MUST justify its benefit and maintenance cost with evidence.

title: Scope limits
normative_text: The initial release MUST NOT claim universal compilation of arbitrary libraries, uniform accelerator access, coherent global memory or instantaneous state migration across vendors. Such capabilities require their own specification and validation.

title: Resource cardinality
normative_text: Configuration MUST admit lists of nodes, execution groups, clusters and providers. It MUST NOT require either a Mac cluster or an NVIDIA cluster as a structural prerequisite. A deployment MAY contain zero instances of either family.

title: Independent roles
normative_text: A machine MAY exercise several authorised roles. Its brand or CPU architecture MUST NOT automatically determine its authority, trust or responsibility for a project.

title: Technical capabilities
normative_text: Resource selection MUST distinguish declared, verified and observed technical capabilities. A detected resource MUST NOT be represented as qualified for every model. Technical capability does not grant permission to use it.

title: Control and data paths
normative_text: Coordination MUST control authorisation and track operations without requiring all files, tensors or results to pass through the coordinator. Direct transfers MUST have their own authorisation and traceability.

title: Resource managers
normative_text: The system MUST support a standalone executor. It MAY integrate managers such as Kubernetes or Slurm through separate contracts. Authority over local reservations MUST be explicit to prevent incompatible allocation of the same resource. [F15] [F16]

title: Execution groups
normative_text: Resources used together for one inference or training operation MUST belong to a group validated for that execution mode. The availability of several destinations for independent tasks MUST NOT prove compatibility for joint computation.

title: Specification
normative_text: TriX MUST have a versioned specification for types, effects, errors, concurrency and distributed execution. The reference implementation MUST be testable against it.

title: Syntax
normative_text: The approved grammar MUST define lexical rules, precedence, associativity and name resolution. Until approval, syntax examples MUST be labelled illustrative. A program MUST NOT change meaning merely because its hardware vendor or operating system changes.

title: Verification
normative_text: The verified core MUST check types before execution. Local type inference MAY be used. Public interfaces MUST expose unambiguous types and contracts. Dynamic operations MUST cross an identifiable boundary.

title: External values
normative_text: Values from models, files, external formats or extensions MUST be validated before use as typed values. Failed conversion MUST produce an identifiable error.

title: Absence and failure
normative_text: The language MUST distinguish a present value, absence and failure. A remote failure MUST NOT implicitly become an empty successful result.

title: Mutability
normative_text: Values SHOULD be immutable by default. Mutation MUST be explicit and follow documented ownership, isolation or synchronisation rules.

title: Resources
normative_text: The language MUST define who controls resource lifetime, when resources may be copied, moved or shared, and how they are released. The final borrowing, reference-counting or other mechanism remains a bounded design decision.

title: Remote memory
normative_text: A local address MUST NOT cross a process or network boundary as a still-valid reference. Transfers MUST use serialisable values or resource identifiers with verifiable validity and authorisation.

title: Effects
normative_text: File, network, process, tool, model and remote-resource operations MUST declare relevant effects. The specification MUST identify static checks and checks performed at access time.

title: Authority capabilities
normative_text: A declaration in a program or extension MUST NOT grant authority by itself. Effect execution MUST depend on capabilities granted and checked by the runtime's authorisation system.

title: Policy propagation
normative_text: Data restrictions MUST survive functions, collections and task boundaries. Reducing restrictions MUST require an explicit, authorised and audited operation.

title: Resource declarations
normative_text: The language MUST distinguish requirements, reservations, enforceable limits, objectives and preferences. Estimates MUST be labelled, and final selection MUST consider observed destination capacity.

title: Concurrency scopes
normative_text: Concurrent constructs MUST define parent-child relationships, scope completion and propagation of failure and cancellation. Work surviving its original scope MUST require an explicit durable-execution operation.

title: Shared state
normative_text: The verified subset MUST specify safe sharing. Actors and messages MAY be used. Messages MUST obey types, authority and data-circulation rules.

title: Cancellation
normative_text: The language MUST distinguish cancellation requested, accepted and actually completed. An expired deadline MUST NOT prove that remote execution stopped.

title: Streams
normative_text: Result streams MUST define ordering, completion, failure and backpressure. Partial output MUST be distinguishable from accepted final output.

title: Intermediate representation
normative_text: Compilation or interpretation MUST produce a verifiable plan containing tasks, dependencies, types, effects and requirements. Its schema MUST be versioned independently of platform binaries.

title: Unknown requirements
normative_text: An executor unable to understand a mandatory requirement MUST reject the task before effects begin. An optional feature MAY be omitted only when the contract permits that alternative.

title: Foreign languages
normative_text: Rust, Python, Swift and other integrations MUST define representations, ownership, object lifetimes, errors, concurrency and cancellation. Process isolation SHOULD be used when extension failure could compromise the core.

title: Guarantee boundary
normative_text: Foreign code, native libraries and binary interfaces MUST NOT implicitly inherit verified-core guarantees. Direct interfaces MUST identify their ABI or protocol and compatible version combinations.

title: Dependencies
normative_text: Modules and extensions MUST have unambiguous identities, versions and dependencies. Installation MUST permit pinning the exact artifacts used. Importing a module MUST NOT increase authority.

title: Reproducibility
normative_text: Tasks MUST be able to declare exact identity, numerical tolerance or quality criteria as their reproduction objective. Relevant versions, configuration and seeds MUST be recorded. Those records alone MUST NOT be represented as proof of identical output.

title: Human authority
normative_text: TriX MUST recognise final human authority over policies, delegation and revocation. Work within current authorisation MUST be able to proceed autonomously without redundant confirmation requests.

title: Context and hierarchy
normative_text: Each task MUST identify its project, issuing authority, scope and policy version. Delegation MUST remain within those bounds. In the reference profile, each project MUST have a SubOrchestrator reporting to the global Orchestrator and a Project Auditor reporting to the Global Auditor, which reports to the human administrator. Coordination MUST NOT subordinate the audit line.

title: Agent channels
normative_text: In the reference governance profile, agents and subagents below the Orchestrator MUST NOT establish autonomous peer-to-peer communication. Delegations and results MUST follow authorised routes. Technical transfers between executors MAY occur without creating autonomous agent channels.

title: Independent audit
normative_text: Auditor identities and permissions MUST be separate from supervised components. Operational credentials MUST NOT authorise modification or deletion of audit evidence or auditor permissions. Authorised administrative changes MUST follow a separate procedure and create verifiable evidence under the published trust model.

title: Enforced policy
normative_text: Authority MUST be checked at relevant access boundaries. Each profile MUST define revocation propagation, cached-authorisation validity and offline behaviour. A received, validated revocation MUST block new affected effects and trigger handling of ongoing work. Offline execution MUST NOT extend previously granted scope or validity.

title: Replicated coordination
normative_text: Replication MUST prevent competing coordinators from causing incompatible accepted allocations or effects over the same resource. Commands carrying stale authority MUST be rejected at the identified enforcement boundary. Recovery MUST preserve work identity and authority.

title: Untrusted content
normative_text: Instructions in documents, model responses and tool outputs MUST NOT become executable policy by themselves. Received content and granted authority MUST remain distinct.

title: Component identity
normative_text: Nodes, coordinators, clients and providers MUST be authenticated on relevant connections. Transport MUST protect integrity and confidentiality under the stated trust model. A node name or task identifier MUST NOT act as an access credential.

title: Secrets and trust
normative_text: Credentials MUST remain outside programs, plans and records not authorised to contain them. The specification MUST publish trust assumptions, including administrator power and isolation limitations.

title: Assurance boundaries
normative_text: The trusted computing base MUST be identified for each assurance claim, including the verifier, enforcement and state components relied upon and relevant host, transport and compilation dependencies. Structural plan verification MUST NOT be treated as proof of source-to-plan semantic preservation. A compromised privileged host may defeat local isolation; the trust model MUST identify which independently controlled audit systems remain trustworthy in that case.

title: Contract
normative_text: Each task MUST declare inputs, outputs, permitted effects, requirements, completion criteria and unavailability behaviour. Models, tools and policies MUST have a version or an explicit resolution rule.

title: Identity
normative_text: Workflows, tasks, attempts and external effects MUST have distinguishable identities. A new attempt MUST NOT erase history or create implicit new authority.

title: States
normative_text: The system MUST distinguish at least created, validated, queued, running, cancelling, succeeded, failed, cancelled and awaiting reconciliation. Reserved, waiting or suspended states MAY be added with defined semantics. Transitions MUST be validated and recorded.

title: Completion
normative_text: Success MUST require verification of the output contract and known effects. A missing response with an uncertain outcome MUST trigger reconciliation when the result cannot otherwise be determined.

title: Retries
normative_text: Retry policy MUST distinguish repeatable computation, idempotent effects and effects requiring reconciliation. TriX MUST NOT promise exactly-once execution for arbitrary external effects.

title: Deduplication
normative_text: Repeatable effects MUST use identification, deduplication or equivalent destination-appropriate mechanisms. Where these do not exist, the task MUST follow an explicit verification or intervention policy.

title: Actual cancellation
normative_text: The executor MUST report whether cancellation is cooperative, stage-dependent or achieved by process interruption. Completed effects MUST remain recorded and MUST NOT be considered undone without confirmation.

title: Checkpoints
normative_text: A checkpoint MUST identify content, versions, resumption unit and compatibility conditions. Logical session state MUST NOT be confused with transferable GPU, process-memory or KV-cache state.

title: Offline continuity
normative_text: Each workflow MUST define loss-of-connectivity behaviour. Offline operation MUST NOT increase authority, export data through an alternative channel or create competing authority over shared resources.

title: Provenance
normative_text: Execution MUST preserve enough evidence to identify code, policies, models, inputs, attempts and results. Recorded content MUST obey access and retention policies.

title: Recovery
normative_text: Each operational profile MUST define recovery objectives, possible progress loss and reconciliation mechanisms. Unmeasured objectives MUST be labelled targets, not operational guarantees.

title: Classification
normative_text: Data and artifacts MUST identify their project, permitted access, authorised destinations and retention policy. These properties MUST be checked during planning and actual access.

title: Derived data
normative_text: Excerpts, summaries, embeddings, transcripts, extracted images and intermediate results MUST retain applicable source restrictions. Reclassification or export MUST be explicit and authorised. Transformation alone MUST NOT be described as automatic anonymisation.

title: Model identity
normative_text: A model MUST be identified to the precision required by the task, including weight revision, tokenizer, format, quantisation, configuration, context and capabilities where relevant. A commercial name alone MUST NOT replace a more precise identity required for reproduction.

title: Substitution
normative_text: Changes to model, quantisation, precision or implementation MUST respect authorised alternatives and quality criteria. Spare capacity or lower cost MUST NOT justify silent substitution.

title: Multimodal data
normative_text: Multimodal inputs and outputs MUST declare relevant formats and limits, including dimensions, duration or volume where applicable. Conversions MUST retain provenance and disclose task-relevant losses.

title: Memory accounting
normative_text: Admission MUST consider relevant weights, caches, buffers, temporaries and operational margin. Estimates MUST distinguish CPU memory, accelerator memory and memory actually shared through a unified architecture.

title: Caches
normative_text: Cache reuse MUST respect model, configuration and data authorisation. Caches MUST NOT provide unauthorised access between projects.

title: Distribution
normative_text: Artifact location, transfers and replicas MUST be explicit. Aggregated memory across nodes MUST NOT be presented as coherent memory available to any process.

title: Consistency
normative_text: The specification MUST define consistency for shared project, artifact and metadata changes. Results under different revisions MUST remain distinguishable. Write conflicts MUST have a documented resolution rule.

title: Retention and deletion
normative_text: The product MUST support retention and deletion policies. It MUST distinguish logical removal, access revocation and physical-erasure guarantees actually supported by the environment.

title: Decision order
normative_text: Prohibited, incompatible or resource-ineligible destinations MUST be excluded before optimisation. Priority, price or performance MUST NOT compensate for a violated mandatory requirement.

title: Limit enforcement
normative_text: A limit MUST be described as enforced only when an appropriate mechanism has been verified. Accounting reservations or usage observations MUST NOT be described as physical isolation.

title: Admission
normative_text: Admission MUST account for quotas, ongoing work and usable capacity. Policies SHOULD protect interactive capacity and prevent indefinite starvation of eligible work.

title: Network and locality
normative_text: Planning MUST consider transfers, latency, bandwidth, data availability and setup costs relevant to the whole workflow.

title: Shared capacity
normative_text: Containers, virtual machines and subsystems exposing the same equipment MUST share a physical-resource identity or equivalent coordination to prevent double counting and over-reservation.

title: Mobility and power
normative_text: Terminals MUST advertise availability, power state and relevant system restrictions. Participation MUST respect user policy and actual ability to continue in the background.

title: External costs
normative_text: Remote operations MUST have a budget and admission policy. Estimates, confirmed charges and uncertain liabilities MUST be distinguishable. A provider's inability to impose a strict cap on an in-flight request MUST be disclosed.

title: Placement explanations
normative_text: The system MUST explain why it selected or excluded a destination without exposing secrets or other projects' data. No eligible destination MUST result in waiting, an error or a previously authorised alternative.

title: Target identity
normative_text: Each package and executor MUST declare the relevant platform combination. Generic labels such as Linux, Windows, ARM or GPU MUST NOT constitute the final compatibility declaration.

title: Observed architecture
normative_text: Inventory MUST distinguish physical architecture, process architecture and native, emulated or virtualised execution. Optional CPU extensions MUST be checked before use.

title: Minimum versions
normative_text: Each release MUST distinguish client, local-execution and feature-specific minima. A compiler's minimum target MUST NOT automatically become the complete product's minimum.

title: Dependencies
normative_text: Python environments and native libraries MUST have pinnable dependencies and compatibility declared by OS, architecture and ABI. Reproducible adapter-specific isolation is RECOMMENDED. [F23]

title: Linux and subsystems
normative_text: Distributions, system libraries and environments such as WSL MUST have separate profiles where they affect execution or acceleration. A container image MUST NOT replace host-driver and resource verification. [F24]

title: Client versus executor
normative_text: Interface support, remote control, local CPU execution, acceleration and distributed computation MUST be classified separately. A fully supported control client MAY lack general local execution.

title: Mobile systems
normative_text: iOS, iPadOS and Android MUST have explicit lifecycle and availability profiles. An installed client MUST NOT be advertised as a permanent executor without supporting mechanisms and conditions. [F07] [F08]

title: Physical validation
normative_text: Cross-compilation and emulation MAY validate parts of the core. Acceleration, energy and performance claims MUST be validated on representative physical hardware.

title: New platforms
normative_text: New targets MUST be addable through platform interfaces and applicable adapters. The central grammar MUST NOT create incompatible vendor-specific dialects.

title: Separate interfaces
normative_text: The design MUST separate platform, accelerator discovery, execution engine, cluster manager and remote-provider interfaces. One extension MAY implement several interfaces while preserving their responsibilities.

title: Minimum execution contract
normative_text: Task-execution adapters MUST expose identity, capabilities, request validation, submission, observation, results and cancellation requests. Other interfaces MUST publish contracts appropriate to their responsibility. Semantics and limitations MUST be explicit; unavailable operations MUST NOT be advertised as supported.

title: Optional operations
normative_text: Reservation, suspension, checkpointing, resumption, state export, priorities and process groups MUST be negotiated. An absent capability MUST NOT be simulated by claiming a stronger guarantee than the implementation provides.

title: Third-party extensions
normative_text: Contract specifications, an SDK, examples and conformance tests MUST be available. A third party MUST be able to add an integration without changing central language semantics.

title: Origin and trust
normative_text: Extensions MUST identify maintainer, version, dependencies and required permissions. Installation and update MUST verify integrity and the defined trust policy for that origin.

title: Model validation
normative_text: Recognising a device or loading an engine MUST NOT qualify every model. Each advertised capability MUST identify its tested scope.

title: Remote models
normative_text: Model APIs MUST obey the same task, data-location, credential, cost and audit contracts. A model-proposed tool call MUST return through local authorisation before execution.

title: Isolation
normative_text: Adapters MUST operate within the authority of assigned work. Failure or restart MUST produce reconcilable errors and states. Separate processes and dependency environments SHOULD reduce interference between engines.

title: Joint computation
normative_text: Splitting one inference or training operation across vendors MUST have a specific backend and tests for operations, communication, precision and recovery. Independent task support MUST NOT be advertised as arbitrary-device tensor parallelism.

title: Version axes
normative_text: Language, plan, protocol, extension API and persistent-state versions MUST be identifiable separately from the product release.

title: Negotiation
normative_text: Components MUST check applicable versions and capabilities before relevant execution. Unknown mandatory features MUST cause explicit refusal. Partial operation MAY occur only where its contract defines it.

title: Releases
normative_text: Each release MUST include target, dependency, integrity, origin and support manifests. Developer tools, clients, executors, adapters and models MUST be independently distributable where their contracts permit it.

title: Updates
normative_text: Updates MUST check compatibility, handle in-flight work and confirm operation before final activation. Gradual activation is RECOMMENDED for execution-affecting changes.

title: Rollback
normative_text: Rollback MUST account for persistent state and checkpoints. Reinstalling an old binary MUST NOT be presented as valid recovery if it cannot interpret the recovered state.

title: Support window
normative_text: Concurrent-version support MUST be explicit and tested. A rule such as current and previous version MAY be claimed only after specifying which components, versions and features it covers.

title: Stability
normative_text: Breaking changes MUST identify impact, migration and treatment of existing programs. Target deprecation MUST state consequences and available alternatives without silently changing task requirements.

title: Support labels
normative_text: The product MUST distinguish project-qualified, maintainer-qualified, qualified with limitations, experimental, remote-client-only and unsupported combinations. Labels MUST apply to specific features and version combinations.

title: Update authenticity
normative_text: Published packages MUST use signatures or equivalent channel-appropriate authenticity. Verification MUST respect authorised keys, revocation and version policy. A valid signature on an old package MUST NOT alone authorise downgrade.

title: Build process
normative_text: Each supported target MUST have a documented, automatable build process identifying tools, SDKs and prerequisites. Restrictions preventing independent reconstruction MUST be documented.

title: Component inventory
normative_text: Distributions MUST preserve an inventory of components, versions, hashes and licences. OS, architecture or ABI variants MUST NOT implicitly share the same binary-dependency set.

title: Artifact reproduction
normative_text: The project MUST check reconstruction in a clean environment. Where byte identity cannot be guaranteed, it MUST declare the verified equivalence level and retain artifact provenance.

title: Essential tools
normative_text: The first usable toolset MUST validate programs or plans, inspect capabilities, run work, observe progress, request cancellation and explain errors. Consistent formatting and editor integration are RECOMMENDED.

title: Diagnostics
normative_text: Errors MUST identify the operation, source location when available, violated requirement and known cause. They MUST distinguish program errors, policy refusal, incompatibility, unavailability and execution failure.

title: Preview
normative_text: The platform MUST inspect a plan without performing its external effects. Preview MUST expose relevant requirements and uncertainties and MUST NOT describe unallocated resources as reserved.

title: Documentation
normative_text: Every stable feature MUST have semantic documentation, executable examples, relevant errors and support conditions. User-facing executable examples MUST be checked against their stated versions.

title: Observability
normative_text: The product MUST expose states, attempts, timings and resource usage. Telemetry and logs MUST minimise private data and respect project permissions.

title: Shared interface contract
normative_text: Clients on different platforms MUST share task, action and state contracts. Visual implementations MAY be platform-specific. Keyboard access, readable messages and status indications independent of colour are RECOMMENDED.

title: Inspectable dependencies
normative_text: Tools MUST expose effective execution versions and permissions. Installation diagnostics SHOULD distinguish installed package, detected device, usable engine and qualified model.

title: Complete examples
normative_text: Documentation MUST include local, cluster and authorised remote-provider workflows and a policy-refusal case. Examples MUST show unavailability and failure behaviour.

title: Web and native access
normative_text: The product design MUST provide a web control application and permit native clients using the same versioned service contracts. A browser client MUST NOT silently obtain native filesystem, process or accelerator authority; any companion bridge MUST be explicitly enrolled and restricted.

title: Accessibility and localisation
normative_text: User interfaces MUST publish an accessibility target and test keyboard operation, focus, screen-reader names and errors. The web reference profile SHOULD target WCAG 2.2 AA. Interface translations MUST preserve operation meanings, units and authority prompts; diagnostic codes MUST remain stable. [F30]

title: Explainable autonomy
normative_text: A client MUST show active delegation scope, relevant limits and task state. Previously granted authority MUST remain usable without repeated prompts. A change requiring more authority MUST identify the concrete new action and reason before requesting it.

title: Decision traces
normative_text: Placement and policy traces MUST record considered constraints and a redacted reason for each decision. Telemetry exports MUST use a declared schema mapping and minimise sensitive payloads. OpenTelemetry conventions MAY be used with pinned versions or commits; changing upstream conventions MUST NOT silently alter TriX evidence fields. [F28]

title: Closed baseline profile
normative_text: The specification MUST publish an exhaustive list of supported value types, expressions, graph constructs, built-in operations and effects for the first subset. Unlisted constructs MUST be rejected or identified as extensions requiring a different declared profile. An extension MUST NOT silently alter baseline semantics.

title: Bounded composition
normative_text: The baseline MUST support acyclic task dependencies, explicit conditional selection and finite collection processing with declared expansion limits. It MUST reject dependency cycles and unbounded plan expansion. General recursion, unrestricted metaprogramming, user-defined kernels and arbitrary native calls are outside this baseline; later support requires an additional specification.

title: Frontend boundary
normative_text: An SDK builder, declarative input and future TriX source frontend MUST produce plans governed by the same semantics. Host-language builder code MUST NOT be treated as verified TriX code. Executing a Python or other builder requires a separately declared build environment and permissions before the resulting plan can be verified.

title: Source specification gate
normative_text: Before a source frontend is stable, its lexical rules, grammar, scope, name resolution, evaluation rules and source-to-plan mapping MUST be published together. The final grammar MAY be selected later. Syntax demonstrations MUST remain labelled illustrative until accepted into that specification and its conformance corpus.

title: Baseline data types
normative_text: The baseline MUST define Boolean, UTF-8 string, byte sequence, signed 64-bit integer, exact finite decimal, typed quantity, immutable record, ordered list, string-keyed map, tagged union, optional value and result value. Each type MUST define construction, equality and serialization. Model tensors MUST declare an external representation and element type rather than inheriting scalar evaluator rules implicitly.

title: Explicit conversions
normative_text: The evaluator MUST NOT apply implicit string-to-number conversions, truthiness conversions or lossy numeric narrowing. Invalid input, absent values and failed operations MUST remain distinguishable. Conversions that can fail MUST return a typed failure. Accepted runtime values MUST conform to the same value rules as source literals.

title: Numeric behavior
normative_text: Integer overflow, division by zero and invalid numeric conversion MUST produce specified errors. Decimal addition and multiplication MUST be exact within declared representation limits; exceeding those limits MUST fail explicitly. Decimal division requiring rounding MUST specify scale and rounding mode. Binary floating-point and tensor operations MUST execute under an explicit engine contract outside the baseline scalar evaluator.

title: Units and budgets
normative_text: Durations, byte quantities, counts and monetary amounts MUST be distinguishable types. Arithmetic MUST reject incompatible units. A monetary amount MUST retain its currency identifier; conversion requires an explicit conversion input. Encodings MUST define base units and scaling, and reject negative or out-of-range values where the field's contract excludes them.

title: Text and ordering
normative_text: Baseline strings MUST be compared by their exact Unicode scalar sequences, without implicit normalization or locale-sensitive comparison. Duplicate map keys MUST be rejected. Map iteration MUST use a documented stable ordering; insertion order MUST NOT become an undeclared dependency. Lists preserve order. Identity and ordering rules MUST remain independent of the host filesystem and locale.

title: Evaluation order
normative_text: The specification MUST define evaluation order and conditional short-circuiting for pure expressions. Task ordering MUST follow explicit dependencies rather than source layout alone. Parallel completion order MUST NOT alter ordered results unless the operation explicitly declares arrival order. Optimizations MUST preserve these observable rules and all required effects.

title: Resource reference model
normative_text: Immutable artifact references MUST identify an object and its representation without themselves granting access. Live allocation handles MUST have an owner, scope, release operation and expiry or invalidation behavior. Copying a resource identifier MUST NOT duplicate an allocation or authorization. The baseline MUST prohibit raw addresses in portable values.

title: Resource consumption
normative_text: Operations that transfer or release exclusive handles MUST consume the corresponding authority exactly as defined by the handle contract. Reuse after confirmed release MUST fail. Failure paths MUST trigger documented cleanup or reconciliation. This is a resource-lifecycle rule; it MUST NOT be presented as a guarantee of immediate cleanup after a disconnected worker fails.

title: Effect composition
normative_text: Each built-in operation and callable module interface MUST expose a machine-readable effect summary. A composed operation MUST conservatively include the effects of its callees and possible branches. A wrapper MUST NOT conceal network access, process creation, model invocation, time access or randomness. Effect declarations describe possible actions and do not grant permission to perform them.

title: Pure planning boundary
normative_text: Parsing, type checking and evaluation of baseline pure expressions MUST NOT perform task effects. Clock, randomness, environment lookup, filesystem discovery and remote inspection MUST be explicit inputs or separately authorized operations. Package acquisition MUST be a visible preparation step. Plan generation MUST NOT run dependency initialization code merely because a declaration is imported.

title: Conservative policy propagation
normative_text: Within baseline verified transformations, an output MUST inherit applicable restrictions from all supplied inputs, including predicates controlling that output. A narrower classification requires the existing explicit reclassification contract. Foreign code MUST use a declared information-flow boundary; the system MUST NOT infer unrestricted output from missing provenance. This rule does not claim elimination of all covert channels.

title: FFI admission and containment
normative_text: Baseline foreign integrations MUST use versioned messages or a documented restricted calling boundary, with validated lengths, representations, ownership and errors. An in-process native extension requires a separately declared trusted profile. Foreign exceptions, panics or equivalent nonlocal exits MUST NOT cross a boundary that does not define them. Native-code access remains subject to the stated trust assumptions.

title: Logical and bound plans
normative_text: The system MUST distinguish a portable logical plan from its execution binding. The logical plan records meaning, requirements and authorized alternatives. Binding records chosen artifacts, model variants, adapters, targets and relevant policy decisions. Late-bound choices MUST produce a resolution record before their effects; they MUST NOT silently mutate the original plan's meaning.

title: Plan invariants
normative_text: Before admission, a separately callable verifier MUST check schema versions, unique node identifiers, reference resolution, graph validity, type compatibility, mandatory fields, declared effects and structural resource bounds. It MUST reject ambiguous encodings, duplicate fields and unsupported mandatory constructs. Validation MUST finish before loading task plugins or starting task effects.

title: Canonical identity
normative_text: The plan specification MUST define canonical semantic encoding and a content digest. Identical source, declared inputs, resolved language dependencies, compiler version and compilation options MUST produce the same logical plan identity. Comments, timestamps, machine paths and display metadata MUST NOT change that identity unless explicitly semantic. Execution attempts and authorizations MUST retain separate identities; a content digest is not an access credential.

title: Verification limits
normative_text: Plan verification MUST state what it proves and what remains for runtime enforcement. It cannot certify arbitrary adapter behavior, available memory, current permission or future numerical quality merely from a manifest. A compiler signature or trusted origin MUST NOT bypass verification. Source-to-plan semantic preservation MUST be validated independently of structural plan validity.

title: Compiler transformations
normative_text: Each optimization MUST preserve data dependencies, errors, effect ordering, policy restrictions and observable results under the declared semantic profile. Transformations that change model, precision, provider or permitted outcomes MUST be explicit planning decisions governed by the task contract, rather than invisible compiler optimizations. An unoptimized reference path MUST remain available for conformance comparisons.

title: Module resolution
normative_text: Imports MUST resolve through declared namespaces and package roots. Ambiguous names, undeclared dependencies and traversal outside approved roots MUST be rejected. Platform-specific implementations MAY share a module contract but MUST identify their target artifacts. Loading an interface declaration MUST NOT execute module initialization or native code.

title: Lockfile contract
normative_text: A release lockfile MUST record the resolved transitive dependency graph, immutable content identities, artifact origins, selected target variants and relevant toolchain identities. Locked builds MUST fail on missing or mismatched artifacts rather than silently selecting alternatives. Permission requirements MAY be recorded for inspection; recording them MUST NOT grant them.

title: Controlled build inputs
normative_text: Release builds MUST declare allowed environment inputs, tool invocations and generated sources. Once declared artifacts are available, verification and construction SHOULD operate without undeclared network access. Required exceptions MUST be recorded in provenance. Native build scripts and SDK builders MUST run with documented authority and MUST NOT be assumed harmless because they run before deployment.

title: Separation of caches and trust
normative_text: Build and compilation cache keys MUST include all inputs that affect generated semantics or target compatibility. Cache reuse MUST verify artifact integrity and the receiving project's access rights. A hit MUST NOT skip required plan verification or current authorization checks. Secret values MUST NOT become public cache identifiers or diagnostics.

title: Structured diagnostics
normative_text: The compiler and verifier MUST emit stable machine-readable error identifiers, severity, phase, relevant plan node and available source locations. Generated code MUST retain a source map to the originating declaration where possible. Human-readable documentation and canonical messages MUST be English; localized presentation MAY coexist without changing error identity or meaning.

title: Inspectable compilation
normative_text: Developer tools MUST expose the normalized logical plan, dependency resolution, effect summary and diagnostics without submitting work. Formatting or source migration tools MUST preserve meaning, or display an explicit semantic change requiring review. Inspection MUST distinguish unresolved choices from fixed bindings and unmeasured estimates from enforced limits.

title: Conformance corpus
normative_text: The language release MUST include positive and negative examples covering each baseline construct and normative edge case. The corpus MUST define accepted values, rejected programs, expected diagnostics and permitted observable traces. At least one reference evaluator or unoptimized execution path MUST support comparison with the production implementation for the verified subset.

title: Stability gate
normative_text: A source-language profile MUST NOT become stable while its grammar, value semantics, source-to-plan mapping or required diagnostics remain unspecified. A plan-only profile MUST define its complete plan encoding, value semantics, semantic invariants and diagnostics before becoming stable; it MUST NOT claim source-language conformance. A release MUST pass its conformance corpus on each claimed implementation target and test malformed or oversized inputs without crashes or unbounded verifier work. Changes to accepted meanings require an identified compatibility decision and updated corpus.

title: Authoritative record
normative_text: Each task MUST have a durable record containing tenant, project, principal, workflow, task and attempt identities; plan and input revisions; authority and policy references; controller epoch; lifecycle state; cancellation intent; output references; and effect records. Updates MUST use an atomic version check or equivalent serialization. Duplicate and reordered messages MUST NOT overwrite newer accepted state.

title: Separate status dimensions
normative_text: The runtime MUST expose the following dimensions independently. A connection failure MUST NOT become evidence that execution stopped or an effect did not occur.

title: Guarded transitions
normative_text: The baseline task lifecycle MUST follow the following transition contract. RUNNING includes an attempt durably authorized for dispatch; actual computation is represented separately. Reservations and suspension MAY extend the model only with documented transition guards and recovery behavior.

title: Terminal decisions
normative_text: Completion and cancellation MUST have a documented serialization point. An acknowledgement that cancellation was requested MUST NOT promise that cancellation won. A deadline expiry MUST NOT imply remote termination. CANCELLED MUST identify the confirmed disposition: execution stopped, or an explicitly permitted alternative that blocks further managed effects while separately tracking ongoing execution and cost. It MUST NOT hide unresolved effects or imply reversal. Terminal decisions MUST preserve evidence and history; contradictory late evidence MUST create a visible correction and incident, prevent unsupported reliance on affected results, and never silently rewrite the past. Explicit follow-up work receives a linked task identity.

title: Workflow boundaries
normative_text: Plans MUST define dependency success conditions, failure propagation, child-task ownership and permitted continuation after parent cancellation. Downstream tasks MUST NOT consume uncommitted results as final outputs. Progressive processing MUST declare its partial-result semantics. Fan-out, recursion, model/tool loops and spawned work MUST remain within explicit policy bounds. Agent delegation continues through the authorized hierarchy.

title: Event evidence
normative_text: Transitions MUST retain event identity, task version, actor, authority epoch, causal references and evidence location. Wall-clock timestamps alone MUST NOT determine distributed event order. Observation freshness, event retention and replay behavior MUST be documented. Replayed notifications MUST NOT repeat task effects.

title: Allocation authority
normative_text: Every exclusive allocation MUST identify its resource scope, owner, validity and monotonically ordered authority epoch. Replicated controllers MUST obtain conflicting ownership decisions through one serialization authority. A single-controller deployment MUST preserve equivalent exclusivity across restart. Controller election alone MUST NOT be treated as proof that previous work can no longer affect resources.

title: Enforcement of stale authority
normative_text: Effect gateways, writable resource boundaries and artifact publication MUST reject stale fencing epochs where fencing is claimed. Checking only the controller's view is insufficient. If a backend cannot fence an accepted operation, the runtime MUST retain that operation as potentially active until reconciled; it MUST NOT claim that a new controller or expired lease revoked the already accepted effect.

title: Lease validity
normative_text: Profiles MUST specify renewal, expiry, allowed clock uncertainty and the behavior of disconnected executors. Uncertain or expired authority MUST block new effects requiring that authority. Local monotonic timers MAY support lease enforcement under declared assumptions. Loss of connectivity MUST NOT extend a lease. Independently authorized offline work MUST use its own bounded allocation and delegation.

title: Controller recovery
normative_text: Recovery MUST reconstruct tasks, attempts, allocations, budget reservations and effects from durable evidence before issuing replacement work. Heartbeat expiry MAY make a resource unavailable for new assignments; it MUST NOT prove that its process stopped. During a partition, exclusivity requirements take precedence over making conflicting assignments available. Unresolved operations remain visible.

title: Effect ledger
normative_text: Before an external request can escape, the runtime MUST persist an effect identity, intent, destination, payload identity and authorization, and mark its outcome potentially UNKNOWN. Repeated submissions of the same logical effect MUST preserve its deduplication identity across attempts. Reuse of that identity with a different payload MUST be rejected. The destination's deduplication scope, retention window and result-query behavior MUST be recorded.

title: Retry admissibility
normative_text: Retry policies MUST bound attempts, elapsed time and resource or financial exposure. Each retry MUST revalidate authority and compatibility. Automatic retry of an uncertain effect is permitted only when the destination's semantics or reconciliation evidence make repetition safe. Switching providers MUST NOT silently convert an uncertain old effect into a fresh independent effect. Exhaustion of a deduplication window requires renewed reconciliation.

title: Qualified guarantees
normative_text: Any exactly-once claim MUST name the transaction domain, failure model and enforcement mechanism. A durable local transaction or outbox alone MUST NOT be presented as exactly-once execution at an arbitrary external destination. Compensation MUST be a separately authorized, identifiable action with its own possible failure and uncertain outcome; compensation does not erase the original effect or establish complete rollback.

title: Publication contract
normative_text: Artifacts MUST distinguish STAGED, VERIFIED, COMMITTED, TOMBSTONED, PURGE_PENDING and PURGED. Normal publication follows STAGED → VERIFIED → COMMITTED. COMMITTED requires validated content identity and atomic visibility of the output reference. Readers MUST reject incomplete or unauthorized artifacts. Abandoned staging data MUST have a cleanup policy. Content integrity alone MUST NOT confer access authority.

title: Retention inventory
normative_text: Each artifact MUST carry ownership, classification, provenance, storage locations, authorized readers, retention policy and applicable holds. The inventory MUST cover replicas, checkpoints, caches, indexes, embeddings, transcripts, thumbnails and other derivatives. Shared storage MUST distinguish a project's reference from shared bytes still legitimately retained for another authorized owner. In-flight readers and references MUST be considered before reclamation.

title: Deletion semantics
normative_text: Deletion MUST distinguish denial of future access, tombstoning, physical purge requests and verified completion within each storage domain. The runtime MUST report inaccessible or disconnected copies and external-provider limitations. It MUST NOT claim recall of bytes already disclosed to an authorized recipient. Retention expiry or deletion MUST prevent prohibited new reuse, including regeneration from retained derivatives, according to the effective policy and revocation window.

title: Backups and restore
normative_text: Backups MUST declare coverage, encryption/key authority, retention, recovery compatibility and possible data loss. Restore MUST reconcile deletion, revocation and policy records before restored data becomes accessible. A recovery environment unable to establish current policy MUST remain restricted. Backup expiry, cryptographic erasure and physical deletion MUST be described separately, with their actual scope and evidence. Restore drills MUST include artifact content and metadata consistency.

title: Identity boundaries
normative_text: Tenant, project, human, service, agent, device and workload identities MUST remain distinguishable. A single-user installation MAY have one tenant but MUST still define its isolation boundary. Task identifiers, artifact digests and node names MUST NOT function as credentials. Authorization MUST bind subject, action, resource, project, delegation scope and validity at each relevant access boundary.

title: Policy context
normative_text: An admitted task MUST retain the policy version used for its decision and obey the documented effect of later revocation or policy changes. Delegated credentials MUST grant only the applicable workload scope; model outputs and external services MUST NOT enlarge it. Audit identities and permissions MUST remain separate from supervised operational identities. Cross-project sharing requires an explicit policy decision.

title: Scheduling contract
normative_text: Admission MUST account for current allocations, queue bounds and relevant CPU, accelerator, memory, storage, transfer and concurrency demands. Policies MUST distinguish eligibility, priority, fairness, preemption and deadlines. Preemption MUST declare whether it loses work, requires a checkpoint or can only terminate a process. Accounting reservations MUST NOT be advertised as physical isolation or guaranteed completion time.

title: Budget ledger
normative_text: Before dispatch, concurrent requests MUST atomically reserve their permitted exposure against the relevant shared budget. The ledger MUST distinguish reserved, incurred, settled and uncertain charges; retries, transfers and external tools must be included where chargeable. Uncertain charges MUST NOT be refunded merely because a response timed out. Strict ceilings require enforceable bounds; otherwise the runtime MUST reject that strict policy or use an explicitly authorized estimated-budget policy.

title: Common control contract
normative_text: Web applications, native clients and automation interfaces MUST share task identity, validation, submission, observation and cancellation semantics. Submission MUST distinguish durable acceptance from execution and completion. Client retries MUST support deduplication; event streams MUST define sequence, reconnect and replay behavior. A transport connection MUST NOT be the sole owner of durable task state.

title: Directional capability contracts
normative_text: Each integration MUST declare inbound and outbound roles separately. An exposed service does not imply authority to invoke external services, and a callback does not grant a new command channel. MCP adapters MUST pin a protocol revision and negotiate or detect capabilities according to that revision; they MUST NOT assume one universal session or handshake model. Bidirectional communication MUST preserve governance and does not authorize autonomous peer-agent communication.

title: Client and transport safety
normative_text: Browser and native clients MUST use an explicit credential and origin trust model. Provider secrets MUST NOT be exposed to a client merely to support remote execution. Inbound credentials MUST NOT be passed through to unrelated downstream services. Callbacks, reconnects and duplicate notifications MUST be authenticated, scoped and replay-safe. Endpoint selection and redirects MUST respect network and data policy.

title: Availability contract
normative_text: Terminal capabilities MUST carry observation time, validity and relevant lifecycle constraints. Suspension, loss of energy or an unreachable device MUST invalidate unsupported availability assumptions. The runtime MUST distinguish best-effort notification, confirmed checkpoint and confirmed stop. Only previously committed state can be relied upon after abrupt loss; a client-only installation MUST NOT be scheduled as a persistent executor.

title: Disconnected operation
normative_text: Each task profile MUST choose among pause, fail, finish already authorized local work, or queue intentions for later admission. Offline execution MUST use bounded local authority, resources and spending allowance established before disconnection. Reconnection MUST preserve identities, reconcile effects and budgets, apply current policy, and resolve conflicting edits without silently overwriting authoritative state. Queued offline intentions are not evidence that remote execution occurred.

title: Declared threat model
normative_text: Each operational profile MUST identify trusted control/state components, independently protected audit components, worker and adapter trust, host administrator powers, and external-provider boundaries. It MUST distinguish accidental failure from malicious behavior. Isolation claims MUST name their mechanism and limits, including shared hosts and accelerators. Untrusted code or data MUST NOT acquire execution authority through deserialization, model instructions or artifact loading.

title: Least-privilege execution
normative_text: Workers and adapters MUST receive only the required artifact handles, secret references, network destinations and operations. A process boundary alone MUST NOT be advertised as an adequate sandbox for hostile code. Unsupported isolation requirements MUST make a destination ineligible. Diagnostics, traces and metrics MUST apply project access rules and avoid exposing credentials or private content through identifiers and error messages.

title: Audit availability
normative_text: Profiles MUST define whether an operation requires durable independent audit acceptance before proceeding. When that condition applies, an audit outage MUST block the operation. Any permitted buffered mode MUST bound its backlog, protect records under the audit trust model and expose delayed or missing evidence. The runtime MUST NOT claim complete independent auditing while required evidence is unavailable.

title: Operational objectives
normative_text: Each release profile MUST declare its recovery-time and recovery-point objectives, authority-staleness bounds, maximum supported queue and artifact sizes, reconciliation policy and capacity assumptions. Numerical values remain design decisions until measured on representative workloads and failure scenarios. No default latency, throughput, lease duration, checkpoint interval or retention period is established by this proposal.

title: Evidence
normative_text: Every applicable mandatory requirement MUST have implementation and validation evidence. A delivery MUST include results, versions, test configuration and known limitations.

title: Correctness
normative_text: Tests MUST cover correct results, expected refusals, isolation, errors and recovery. Model quality MUST be evaluated against task-specific criteria.

title: Performance
normative_text: Comparisons MUST identify model, revision, precision, quantisation, context, concurrency and hardware. Startup and preparation MUST be distinguished from execution with a loaded model. Measurements MUST support assessment of latency, capacity, memory, energy where available and cost per useful completed work.

title: Real failures
normative_text: Distributed profiles MUST be evaluated under process, node and network interruptions, availability changes and uncertain external outcomes. Tests MUST check that the system neither invents completion nor blindly repeats effects.

title: Demonstrated extensibility
normative_text: Before claiming operational vendor independence, the project MUST demonstrate a third real integration beyond the two reference configurations through the published extension contracts. Simulations MAY aid development but MUST NOT substitute for that evidence.

title: Release gate
normative_text: A stable release MUST pass applicable scenarios and resolve defects violating mandatory requirements. Incomplete functionality MUST remain explicitly experimental or unavailable.

title: Bounded claims
normative_text: Every qualification claim MUST identify the specification revision, component build, role, operation, platform profile, workload profile, and applicable requirements. Client control, CPU execution, accelerated execution, remote access, and joint distributed computation MUST be qualified separately. A successful benchmark MUST NOT establish conformance for untested operations.

title: Lifecycle and ownership
normative_text: Profiles MUST carry a lifecycle state, accountable maintainer, execution role, limitations and applicable review triggers. A qualified claim MUST additionally identify its validating party, evidence reference and qualification date. Planned profiles MAY leave qualification-specific fields unset, explicitly indicating that qualification has not occurred. Lifecycle, execution role, validating party and limitations MUST remain separate fields, refining VER-008 rather than conflating these dimensions.

title: Measured environment
normative_text: Qualification MUST record an actual hardware and software snapshot. Minimum OS versions for the application, local execution, and individual features MUST be declared separately. Missing measurements MUST remain unknown, never inferred from a vendor name. Provider-managed hardware may be undisclosed; the resulting claim MUST be bounded to the observed service contract and revision.

title: Predetermined gates
normative_text: Each workload profile MUST define its metrics, units, thresholds, sampling method, observation window, failure denominator, and decision rule before acceptance measurements begin. Unset thresholds MUST block qualification for the affected claim. Targets MUST be labelled as targets until measured; no default numerical targets are established here.

title: Experimental discipline
normative_text: Evaluations MUST fix workload revisions, configuration, preparation, repetition and sampling rules. Development, evaluator calibration, and held-out acceptance sets MUST be separated. Cold startup, model loading, compilation, cache effects, and warm execution MUST be reported separately. Seeds, sample counts, variation, exclusions, and measurement uncertainty MUST be retained. Insufficient evidence produces an inconclusive result rather than a pass.

title: Non-AI conformance
normative_text: Compiler, interpreter, planner, and runtime correctness MUST have machine-checkable oracles independent of language-model opinion. Tests MUST cover the adopted grammar or plan schema, name/type/effect rules, serialization, resource lifetime, error propagation, concurrency, cancellation, stream ordering, backpressure, and state transitions. Differential or metamorphic testing SHOULD supplement independently specified expected behaviour. Unspecified semantics MUST be resolved before the affected conformance claim.

title: Limited evaluator authority
normative_text: An AI judge MAY assist task-quality assessment where objective checks are insufficient. It MUST NOT override type checks, numerical gates, authorization, confidentiality, state invariants, or evidence integrity. Evaluator inputs MUST follow the same data-location and access policies as the tested workload.

title: Calibration
normative_text: Before a judge affects acceptance, its rubric, prompt, model/revision, sampling settings, and tools MUST be versioned and assessed against independently human-labelled examples. Calibration MUST cover relevant task slices, difficult failures, disagreement, abstention, order effects, and instructions embedded in candidate answers. Labels and adjudication rationales MUST be retained. Agreement and error tolerances MUST be declared in advance, with adequate sampling and uncertainty analysis.

title: Adjudication
normative_text: Where an AI judge contributes to qualitative acceptance, the decision MUST combine applicable objective checks, calibrated qualitative scores and the profile's predetermined decision rule. Profiles using sufficient objective criteria alone do not require an AI judge. Judge disagreement, an indeterminate boundary result, suspected evaluator manipulation, or insufficient confidence MUST trigger the defined human review path. Human adjudication resolves qualitative ambiguity against the rubric; it cannot waive a failing mandatory conformance gate. A judge revision or material drift requires recalibration and impact assessment.

title: Test catalogue
normative_text: Tests MUST identify applicable requirements, profile, fixtures, stimulus, oracle, expected effects, and evidence. The catalogue MUST distinguish unit/static checks; property, fuzz, and metamorphic tests; schema/ABI interoperability; adapter integration; distributed fault injection; security/policy tests; model quality; performance/soak; client lifecycle; installation; and recovery. A mock result MUST be labelled as such.

title: CI gates
normative_text: Each change MUST run deterministic checks and the tests affected by its contracts. Hardware-dependent suites MUST run against registered snapshots before releasing affected support claims. Scheduled campaigns SHOULD cover longer fuzzing, soak, load, and failure exploration. Release candidates MUST pass their declared profile matrix, update/recovery paths, and applicable CA scenarios. Skipped, blocked, and not-applicable results MUST remain distinct; a skipped mandatory test cannot count as a pass.

title: Work sequence
normative_text: Implementers MUST select the profile and requirement mapping, register fixtures and expected outcomes, capture the environment, build from identified sources, run checks, investigate failures, and publish an evidence manifest before requesting qualification. Existing valid evidence MAY be reused only with a recorded impact rationale. Review MUST include an accountable verifier distinct from the change author for promotion to qualified.

title: Event records
normative_text: Qualification MUST produce structured records linking requirements, tests, builds, profiles, tasks, attempts, and effects where relevant. Records MUST distinguish observation, inference, and verdict. UTC timestamps support correlation; monotonic durations support local timing. Event ordering across machines MUST NOT rely solely on unsynchronised wall clocks.

title: Reproduction package
normative_text: Evidence MUST include source/build identity, dependency locks, configuration, snapshot, fixture revisions, commands, raw permitted measurements, summarisation method, verdicts, and protected artifact hashes. An independent authorised reviewer MUST be able to rerun or audit the claim. Proprietary or unavailable dependencies MUST be identified, with the resulting reproducibility limitation. Evidence retention and access follow project policy.

title: Defect handling
normative_text: Every failing mandatory gate MUST create a tracked defect with scope, owner, reproducer, remediation, and closure evidence. Unauthorized effects, protected-data exposure, state corruption, false completion, or invalid update acceptance MUST stop affected qualification and rollout. Flaky tests require investigation; retry history MUST be retained and a later pass MUST NOT erase an unexplained failure. Quarantining a test cannot preserve an unsupported qualification claim.

title: Controlled promotion
normative_text: Release plans MUST identify candidate artifacts, authentication checks, deployment cohorts, health signals, exposure limits, stop rules, and recovery actions. Promotion proceeds from laboratory evidence to an authorised limited deployment and then broader rollout. Cohort sizes and observation windows are profile decisions. Shadow evaluation MUST NOT duplicate external effects or export protected data without authorization.

title: State-aware recovery
normative_text: Qualification MUST exercise upgrade interruption, mixed-version operation where offered, state/checkpoint migration, backup restoration, and offline-node return. Recovery MUST verify schema compatibility, task/effect identities, authority, and audit continuity before resuming work. Binary rollback alone is insufficient. Irreversible migration requires a tested compatible restore or forward-recovery procedure, with declared data-loss implications.

title: Stop and resume
normative_text: Operational acceptance MUST define thresholds for stopping promotion, withdrawing affected capabilities, or entering controlled recovery. Resumption requires a recorded cause assessment, corrective action, affected-scope revalidation, and the designated approval. Existing authorized routine execution does not require repeated human confirmation. The supported-version window, including any N/N-1 policy, remains an explicit pending decision until approved and tested.

title: Contract artefacts
normative_text: The adopted specification MUST publish schemas for public records, examples that validate against them, rejection cases, version rules and semantic invariants not expressible by the schemas. Structural validation MUST NOT be presented as proof of authority, graph correctness, provider behaviour or physical capability.

title: Record boundaries
normative_text: Requests MUST distinguish project and task identities, operation reference, input and output contracts, requested effects, data policy, resource requirements, retry policy and completion criteria. Authority references MUST be opaque references to verifiable grants, never embedded provider credentials or self-issued authority.

title: Structural encoding
normative_text: Revision 0.2 companion JSON records MUST reject duplicate keys, non-finite numeric literals, unknown top-level fields and malformed required values. Extensible metadata MUST use declared namespaced keys. Unknown mandatory features MUST be rejected by semantic admission even when their strings are structurally valid. Encoded 64-bit integers and exact decimals MUST avoid implicit conversion through binary floating-point.

title: Semantic checks
normative_text: The production verifier MUST additionally check identifier uniqueness, resolved dependencies, acyclicity where required, type compatibility, operation/effect correspondence, quantity bounds, policy relationships and supported mandatory features. The package validator checks documentation records and selected discriminating fixtures only; it MUST NOT be advertised as that production verifier.

title: API specification
normative_text: Before an inbound API is stable, the project MUST publish a machine-readable API definition covering authentication context, request/response schemas, errors, pagination, resource limits, idempotency, asynchronous states and event recovery. The API MUST expose an API version distinct from product and language versions. A client retry MUST reuse its submission identity for the same payload; changed payload under that identity MUST be rejected.

title: Credential lifecycle
normative_text: API keys or other credentials MUST have an identified issuer, subject, project scope, permitted operations, creation, expiry, revocation and rotation rules. Secrets MUST be stored in an appropriate protected facility and shown only through authorised workflows. Long-lived provider credentials MUST remain on the authorised service or executor boundary rather than being copied into browser bundles, plans or general logs.

title: Events and errors
normative_text: An API MUST distinguish durable acceptance from execution and verified completion. Event subscriptions MUST expose a resumable cursor or a documented snapshot-reconciliation mechanism, duplicate handling and retention limits. Errors MUST contain a stable code, category, correlation identifier and safe remediation; retryability MUST state conditions rather than promise that retry cannot duplicate an effect.

title: MCP adapters
normative_text: The reference integration design MUST support both exposing an authorised subset of TriX through an MCP server and consuming external MCP servers through an MCP client. Each direction MUST have separate permissions and pinned protocol revisions. Capability availability MUST follow that revision's rules. Tool descriptions, resources and returned content MUST remain untrusted data. Local process launch, token audience, callback validation, endpoint redirects and outbound network access MUST follow the boundary threat model. [F25] [F26]

title: Portability and exit
normative_text: Projects MUST be exportable with their logical definitions, dependency references, policies, allowed artifacts and provenance in documented formats. Export MUST enforce access and retention policies, identify omitted provider-owned or unavailable content, and exclude secret values by default. Import MUST revalidate identities, dependencies and authority; a successful export MUST NOT imply that a different infrastructure can execute every operation.

title: Extension evolution
normative_text: Adapter SDKs MUST publish required and optional operations, error taxonomy, ownership, concurrency and shutdown contracts, supported API revisions and a conformance harness. A capability removal or changed effect summary MUST trigger compatibility review. An extension's integrity signature MUST NOT be treated as evidence that it is correct, safe or qualified.

title: Vertical delivery
normative_text: From E1 onward, every implementation stage MUST deliver at least one usable end-to-end flow with observable errors and limitations. E0 MUST produce complete specified scenarios traceable to requirements. Later stages MUST NOT depend on capabilities announced as stable without evidence.

title: Later grammar
normative_text: The source grammar and tools MUST preserve validated prototype contracts or document migration. Syntax creation MUST NOT conceal semantic changes.

title: Pending decisions
normative_text: Each pending decision MUST have an accountable role, resolution gate and decision record. User- or extension-affecting choices MUST stabilise before public compatibility promises.

title: Implementer handoff
normative_text: Each work item MUST name its applicable requirements, acceptance cases, dependencies, owner role, artifacts and completion evidence. Parallel work MUST use an agreed contract revision and an identified integration owner. A merge MUST NOT silently change another team's contract.

title: Controlled iteration
normative_text: Implementers MUST preserve failed observations, diagnose the violated contract, add a discriminating regression where needed, implement a correction and rerun affected gates. They MUST NOT change expected outcomes, reduce scope invisibly or delete failures merely to produce a pass. Experiments MUST have a resource budget and stopping rule; exhausted or blocked work MUST report the concrete blocker and evidence.

title: Release evidence
normative_text: Each release candidate MUST provide requirement coverage, complete applicable test results, unresolved defects, dependency inventory, qualified profiles, migration/recovery procedures and an accountable review. Missing evidence MUST remain distinguishable from a passing result.

title: Operational ownership
normative_text: Before operational acceptance, each deployed component MUST have an owner role, monitoring and incident route, credential/revocation procedure, backup/recovery procedure and maintenance policy. The operating model MUST state who can stop, restore or re-enable affected capabilities under existing delegation.

title: Extension and licence governance
normative_text: Before public distribution, the project MUST record licences for the specification, reference code, SDK, examples and contributed extensions; contribution and vulnerability-reporting procedures; release authority; and package-name/ownership rules. Third-party model and SDK conditions MUST be identified for the particular distributed artifact. This requirement does not select a licence or imply rights not yet granted.

title: Documentation maintenance
normative_text: Specification, schemas, registries, examples and generated documents MUST identify the same release baseline or an explicit compatibility relationship. Published changes MUST update the change log and migration notes. All released documentation MUST follow IDN-005. Outdated documents and examples MUST identify their superseded status.
